title: Throughput SLA templates, error-budget matrix, and breach remediation playbook for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Provide a set of concrete, lawyer-friendly SLA templates and an operational error-budget methodology specific to Redwood Dedicated capacity. The deliverable includes measurement rules, example calculations, automated monitoring hooks, and a prescriptive remediation/credit model that legal and sales can include in customer contracts. This doc favors operational measurability (machine-checked signals) and predictable indemnity caps rather than vague language.
acceptance_criteria: SLA template text passed by legal review (clauses for measurement, exclusions, credits, and termination thresholds)
Error budget calculation documented and implementable from telemetry (Prometheus/Grafana query examples)
Breach playbook with clear on-call and customer notification steps vetted with SRE and Support
Telemetry dashboards and alert rules (raw queries) committed to infra repo and smoke-tested against historical incidents
sla_text_proposed: SLA summary (customer-facing): Redwood guarantees that a customer's Dedicated capacity pool will deliver at least the Provisioned Throughput Entitlement (PTE) for a rolling evaluation window of 30 minutes, 99% of the time in a monthly billing cycle. 'Provisioned Throughput Entitlement (PTE)' is defined in the customer's order form as X Throughput Entitlement Units (TEU) where 1 TEU equals 1,000 model tokens-per-second of provisioned serving capacity at the configured service level. Measurement and exclusions are defined below. If Redwood fails to meet the PTE in aggregate beyond the error budget (see Error Budget section), Customer is eligible for Service Credits as described in the Credits Schedule. Remedies are limited to Service Credits and do not include consequential damages. Service Credits will be applied as a percentage of the monthly Dedicated fee for the impacted capacity pool, subject to the maximum liability cap described in the agreement.
error_budget_definition: Core idea: measure throughput shortfall in TEU-minutes over the monthly window and translate to an error budget burned percentage. Definitions: 1) Provisioned Throughput Entitlement (PTE): TEU provisioned and listed in the contract. 2) Measurement interval: 1 minute sampling from platform metrics. 3) Shortfall in a minute = max(0, PTE - observed_effective_throughput_minute). Observed_effective_throughput_minute uses smoothed token-rate accounting that excludes retries and client-side rate limits. 4) Monthly entitlement in TEU-minutes = PTE * number_of_minutes_in_month. 5) Error Budget Burned (%) = (Sum of shortfalls across the month in TEU-minutes) / Monthly_entitlement * 100. Thresholds (example template): - Green: Burned <= 1% -> no credits. - Yellow: 1% < Burned <= 3% -> 10% monthly credit. - Red: Burned > 3% -> 30% monthly credit and joint remediation plan required. Example: PTE=100 TEU, month=43200 minutes, monthly_entitlement=4,320,000 TEU-minutes. If sum(shortfalls)=129,600 TEU-minutes -> Burned = 3% -> triggers Red tier. Important: measurements exclude force majeure, customer's misconfiguration, and scheduled maintenances announced >72h in advance.
measurement_and_monitoring: Telemetry sources and queries: - Primary metric: dedicated.pool.<pool_id>.effective_token_rate (tokens/sec) sampled per minute. - Conversion to TEU: effective_token_rate / 1000 = TEU. - Minute-level measurement: effective_TEUs_min = floor((tokens/sec averaged across minute) / 1000). - Shortfall series calculation demo (PromQL-like pseudo): sum_over_month(max(0, (PTE - effective_TEUs_min))) * 1 minute = TEU-minutes shortfall. - Data retention and reconciliation: authoritative source is the billing dataset derived from the serving runtime's aggregated throughput logs (S3 partitioned by month). - SLO windowing: rolling 30-minute eligibility used for operational alerts; monthly window used for contract calculations. - Automated alerts: when 30-minute rolling shortfall > 0.5% of PTE for 3 consecutive evaluation windows, create P1 ticket and start customer notification cadence. - Observability hooks: add dedicated dashboard with minute histogram, cumulative TEU-minutes shortfall, and computed Error Budget Burned percent. - Measurement caveats: exclude minutes flagged for scheduled maintenance, customer traffic below minimum baseline (see 'minimum utilization exclusion' below), and retries caused by upstream client throttling recorded in request metadata.
breach_playbook: Detect: Alert fires from monitoring rule (30-min rolling shortfall > 0.5% for 3 windows)
Triage (0-30m): SRE on-call acknowledges, captures runbook snapshot, and identifies whether impact is kernel/host/network/orchestration
Notify (within 60m): Send initial incident email to customer success and named contacts with basic impact, ETA for next update, and mitigation steps if available

Mitigate (0-4h): If root cause is autoscaling delay, manually trigger scale-up or emergency burst policy; if kernel-level, activate safe-fallback model variant to preserve throughput while degrading quality
Remediate (4h-72h): Track incident, determine code/config/root cause, implement patch or capacity change, run regression tests on canary pool
Post-incident (72h-14d): Joint postmortem with customer if requested, calculate exact TEU-minutes shortfall for contract credit computation, propose remediation plan and ETA
Apply Credits (monthly billing): Calculate service credits according to Error Budget burn tier and apply to next invoice. Credits are the sole financial remedy unless otherwise agreed in contract
Escalation: If repeated Red-tier breaches occur in 3 consecutive months, Sales + Legal will discuss contract re-pricing, additional reserved capacity, or termination rights as per contract clause
pricing_and_credit_model: Suggested credit schedule (template): - Burned <= 1.0%: 0% credit - 1.0% < Burned <= 2.0%: 10% credit of monthly Dedicated fee for affected pool - 2.0% < Burned <= 3.0%: 20% credit - Burned > 3.0%: 30% credit, plus mandatory remediation plan and bi-weekly executive sync until healthy. Caps and limits: Credits capped at 100% of the monthly fee for the impacted pool. Maximum liability for throughput SLA breaches is limited to 3x monthly fees for the affected pool per rolling 12-month period. Rationale: balanced incentives—small fluctuations produce no credit; sustained shortfalls result in meaningful credits and operational escalation. Sales may offer custom tiers for strategic customers with alternative caps and termination options.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Legal review and sign-off on SLA template language and credits schedule
Week 2: Instrumentation: commit PromQL/metrics queries and dashboard templates to infra repo; add alerting rules
Week 3: Run retrospective simulations against the last 12 months of telemetry to sanity-check thresholds and false-positive rate
Week 4: Pilot with two internal customers and one external beta customer for 1 billing cycle
Week 5: Finalize docs, publish to customer contracts playbook, and enable as default for new Dedicated orders unless negotiated
notes: Decision: Use TEU (token-rate normalized) for throughput accounting rather than RPS to align with multi-model token cost variability
Trade-off: Minute-level sampling is susceptible to spikes; smoothing chosen to prioritize measurability and low noise for legal defensibility
Feedback from SRE: Excluding scheduled maintenances must require explicit calendar entry to prevent misuse
Pending: Legal wants explicit clause for disagreement resolution on measurement; propose tie-breaker: third-party metric auditor or agreed reconciliation dataset

Follow-up: Add a clause for 'Minimum Utilization Exclusion' so customers that provision but never send traffic are not eligible for credits; define minimum as average utilization >= 2% of PTE over billing cycle
